instruction: Create a desktop shortcut for this YouTube page so I can access it directly from my desktop. Use Chrome's shortcut tool.

rules.name: Rick Astley - Never Gonna Give You Up (Official Music Video)

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a desktop shortcut for a YouTube video page using Chrome's built-in shortcut feature. The evaluator checks for a .desktop file on the desktop with the correct Exec line containing the app-id for the YouTube page.
metadata.verification: Reused existing is_shortcut_on_desktop metric and shortcuts_on_desktop getter. Checks for shortcut name matching the YouTube video title instead of hardcoded app-id to avoid Chrome's deterministic but environment-specific app-id generation.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: shortcuts_on_desktop (chrome.py:1084) properly reads .desktop files from desktop directory and returns their content as a dictionary mapping {shortcut_path: file_content_string}

Metric logic is correct: is_shortcut_on_desktop (chrome.py:487) with type='name' checks if 'Name=<expected_name>\n' exists in any shortcut file content, which correctly verifies the shortcut was created
Expected value is semantically correct: 'Rick Astley - Never Gonna Give You Up (Official Music Video)' is the actual YouTube video title for URL https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ
Verification approach is robust: Using name matching instead of app-id matching avoids Chrome's environment-specific app-id generation issues while still semantically verifying task completion

Coverage is complete: Verifies that a desktop shortcut exists with the correct YouTube page title, which semantically confirms the core instruction requirement (creating a desktop shortcut for the YouTube page)
Data flow is correct: Getter extracts .desktop file content from filesystem → Metric checks for Name field match with exact string comparison → Expected value matches actual video title
Postconfig is adequate: 2-second sleep is sufficient for filesystem write operations; no UI reopening needed since getter reads from disk, not UI state

Acceptable limitations: Does not verify shortcut points to correct URL or is Chrome-specific, but this is acceptable because only Chrome creates web page shortcuts with the page title as the Name field in Linux .desktop files. The combination of specific video title + .desktop file is sufficient to verify task completion
Edge cases handled: Empty shortcuts dictionary would return 0.0 (task not completed), which is correct behavior
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional enhancement: Could add secondary check for Exec line containing 'google-chrome' or 'chromium' to ensure it's a Chrome shortcut
Optional enhancement: Could add check for 'StartupWMClass' field which is specific to Chrome web app shortcuts for extra validation
Optional enhancement: Could verify the shortcut Exec line contains the YouTube URL to ensure it points to the correct page
